Venue.includes: The hall itself, with tables and chairs included — you'll still need to meet the venue's minimum food & beverage spend separately.
A reserved section of the restaurant closed off for your group, with its own seating and privacy from other diners.
Exclusive use of the rooftop/terrace space for your event duration — no outside guests sharing the area.
The outdoor grounds or lawn itself for your event — you'll arrange tenting, catering and power separately.
The hotel's banquet hall for your event duration, typically with in-house AV points and backup power.
The community or club hall space, usually with basic chairs/tables already in place.
A reserved dining area set aside just for your group within a restaurant or club.
A refundable deposit held by the venue against any damage — returned after the event if nothing's broken.
The venue's mandatory cleaning charge for after your event — separate from any decorator cleanup.

Furniture.includes: Simple plastic chairs for guest seating — the most basic, budget option.
Cushioned, upholstered chairs that look more formal than plastic — common for banquet-style seating.
Elegant wood or clear acrylic chairs often seen at weddings — the upgrade look for a head table or stage.
Round dining tables seating 6-10 guests each, for buffet or plated meal seating.
Rectangular tables for buffet lines, gift tables or long-seating arrangements.
A sofa-and-coffee-table lounge cluster for a relaxed seating corner, separate from dining seating.
Tall standing tables for a cocktail-hour or mingling area, no chairs included.
A fitted cloth cover for your tables in your chosen colour, hiding the bare table underneath.
A fabric cover (often with a sash) that dresses up plain chairs for a more finished look.
Plates, cutlery and glasses for each guest — what's actually on the table when food is served.

Catering.includes: A self-serve vegetarian buffet with a set number of dishes — the main food guests eat.
A self-serve buffet including non-vegetarian dishes alongside the vegetarian spread.
A selection of passed or counter-served starters/appetizers before the main meal.
A complete buffet spanning starters, mains, breads and dessert — the full spread, not just one course.
A formal, waiter-served meal brought to each guest's table course by course, instead of a buffet line.
An afternoon spread of tea/coffee with light snacks and bites — not a full meal.
A morning buffet of breakfast items — for events that start early in the day.
A late-morning buffet blending breakfast and lunch dishes.
A live chaat station with a chef preparing 1-3 chaat items fresh in front of guests.
A live counter where pasta is cooked to order in front of guests, not pre-made.
A live station making fresh pizzas on the spot, often with a visible oven setup.
A live momos counter steaming/frying momos fresh for guests.
A live dosa counter with a chef making dosas to order.
A standing tea/coffee station guests can visit throughout the event.
A non-alcoholic drinks counter with a bartender mixing mocktails to order.
Unlimited juice and soft drinks served throughout the event.
Waitstaff to serve food, clear plates and assist guests through the meal.
A chef on-site cooking and/or serving live, rather than food arriving pre-made.

Bar.includes: A bartender mixing and serving drinks at your bar setup.
The physical bar counter/station itself, styled to match your event.
Glasses for serving drinks to each guest at the bar.

Decor.includes: A backdrop wall built from balloon clusters in your chosen colours — what guests see behind the cake table or photo spot.
An organic, cloud-style balloon backdrop with varied sizes and extra styling details — a fuller, more designed look than the basic version.
A backdrop built with real fresh flowers instead of balloons — a more premium, fragrant look that needs same-day setup.
A dense wall entirely covered in flowers (artificial or fresh), popular as a photo backdrop.
Decor for the venue entrance — the first thing guests see when they arrive, styled in balloons, florals or your theme.
A decorative arrangement placed at the centre of each table — flowers, candles or themed props.
Draping, balloons or florals installed overhead to dress up the ceiling/roof line of the venue.
A standee or easel board with a welcome message and the celebrant's name, placed near the entrance.
A custom-made neon or LED sign spelling out a name or message, used as a backdrop or photo prop.
Hats, glasses, signs and other handheld props guests use for photos, plus a simple backdrop.
Flowing fabric panels used as a backdrop or ceiling drape, a softer alternative to a balloon/floral wall.

Cake.includes: A simple cake in your chosen flavour and colour theme, serving roughly 10-25 guests depending on size.
A cake with detailed custom design work — fondant figures, intricate piping or a themed shape, not just icing.
A cake with an edible print of a photo on top — the celebrant's picture or a chosen image.
A small single-serve cake, usually personalised with a short message — popular for intimate celebrations.
Individually decorated cupcakes, sold per piece — good for favours or alongside a smaller main cake.
A styled table of assorted mini desserts (tarts, jars, macarons) beyond just the cake.
A decorative topper — name, age number or themed figure — placed on top of the cake.

Photography.includes: A photographer covering your event for an agreed number of hours, delivering edited photos afterward.
A second photographer shooting alongside the main one, for wider coverage or multiple angles at once.
A videographer filming the event, delivered as raw or cinematically edited footage depending on tier.
A short, music-set highlight video of the event, edited for sharing on social media.
A physical printed photo album of selected event pictures, delivered after editing.
An instant-print photo station/camera so guests get a physical photo to take home same day.
A dedicated photo booth with backdrop and props guests can use to take their own fun photos.
A rotating camera platform that films guests in a 360° slow-motion video, with an operator running it.
Aerial photos/video of the venue and event shot by a drone operator.

Entertainment.includes: A host who runs the event flow — announcements, games, keeping energy up between segments.
A singer (solo or with one accompanist) performing live through the event.
A stripped-down acoustic performer (guitar/keys + vocals), suited to a mellower, background-music vibe.
A full band performing live sets — bigger sound and stage presence than a solo singer.
A group of trained dancers performing a choreographed act, not audience participation.
A stand-up comedian performing a set tailored to your crowd — a dedicated entertainment slot.
A magician performing tricks/illusions as a dedicated show segment, often popular at kids' events.
A costumed character (cartoon/theme mascot) and the performer inside it, for photos and interaction with kids.
An entertainer doing balloon twisting, games or clowning specifically to engage younger guests.
An artist painting designs on guests' faces throughout the event — a popular kids' activity station.
A karaoke machine with song library and mic, plus someone running it so guests can sing.

Activities.includes: One staffed interactive game stall (ring toss, etc.) guests can play at during the event.
Tambola tickets, numbered calling and a host to run rounds of housie as a group activity.
An inflatable bouncy castle with an attendant supervising kids while they play.
A fenced soft-play zone with cushioned equipment for toddlers and young kids.
A pit filled with plastic balls for younger kids to play in — standalone or a soft-play add-on.
Gaming consoles connected to a screen so guests can play video games during the event.
VR headsets and an operator guiding guests through a virtual-reality experience.
Basic sports equipment (bats, nets, cones) set up for a casual game at the venue.

AV & Production.includes: A large LED video wall for visuals, slideshows or branding, with basic rigging support included.
A projector and screen for slideshows, videos or presentations during the event.
Speakers sized to your guest count, set up and connected for music/announcements.
A handheld or lapel wireless microphone for speeches, hosting or performances.
An audio mixer to balance multiple sound sources (mics, music, speakers) live.
A raised platform for performers, speakers or the main table to stand above the crowd.
A metal truss framework used to rig lights, banners or branding above the stage/venue.
A technician operating the sound and lighting equipment live through the event.

Special Effects.includes: A fog/haze machine (plus someone operating it) used to add atmosphere for entries or performances.
A machine that continuously blows bubbles, popular at kids' events or for photo moments.
A confetti cannon/machine for a celebratory burst moment — cake cutting, entry, or the big reveal.
Fountain-style cold spark machines (safe indoors) for a dramatic entrance or stage moment.
Laser light effects synced to music, adding a club/concert feel to the dance floor.
A machine producing fake snow for a themed, wintery atmosphere.

Stage & Branding.includes: A free-standing printed cutout/poster, used for photos, directions or branding.
A branded backdrop with repeated logos/names, the classic red-carpet-style photo wall.
A set of printed signs guiding guests — directions, welcome message, menu labels.
A standing podium/lectern for speeches or formal announcements.

Invitations.includes: A designed digital invitation card/image you can share on WhatsApp or social media.
A short animated (motion graphics) version of your invite, more eye-catching than a static image.
A short video invitation with visuals and audio, sent digitally instead of a card.
Physical printed invitation cards to hand-deliver or mail to guests.
Tracking who's confirmed, declined or hasn't responded yet, so you know your real headcount.

Stationery.includes: A standee welcoming guests by name at the entrance — simpler and more printed than the decor-category version.
A printed card listing the meal/menu, placed at each table or buffet station.
A numbered card/stand marking each table, so guests can find their seats.
A small card with each guest's name, marking their assigned seat.
A master board/chart near the entrance showing which table each guest is seated at.

Gifting.includes: A small gift given to child guests as they leave — the classic birthday-party return favour.
A take-home gift for adult guests, a step up from kids' party favours.
A pre-assembled hamper of curated items (sweets, snacks, small gifts) in one package.
A hamper that can carry your company branding, for office events or client gifting.
A gift customised with a name, photo or message, rather than a generic item.
Professional gift-wrapping service for items you're giving or guests are bringing.
Delivery of gifts/hampers to guests' addresses instead of handing them out in person.

Makeup & Styling.includes: Event-ready makeup application for one person, lighter than bridal makeup.
A styled hairdo for the event — blow-dry, updo or curls depending on the look.
A stylist draping your saree or dupatta for you, so it sits correctly and stays in place.
A grooming session covering hair styling, beard trim or basic grooming before the event.

Logistics.includes: Transport of decor/catering materials from the vendor to your venue.
Labour to load and unload equipment/materials at the venue, usually bundled with bigger setups.
A vehicle (and driver) shuttling guests to/from the venue, e.g. from a parking area or hotel.
Valet staff parking and retrieving guests' cars so they don't have to self-park.

Manpower.includes: Someone managing vendors and timing on the day, so you're not running the event yourself.
Oversight staff making sure setup and service run to plan, reporting issues as they happen.
Labour hands who physically assemble decor/furniture/equipment before the event starts.
Labour hands who take everything down and clear out after the event ends.
Security personnel managing entry, crowd and venue safety.
Staff doing ongoing cleaning during the event (spills, washrooms, trash) — separate from the post-event cleanup.
Staff checking guests in and guiding them to seating or activities.

A water-based air cooler for outdoor or non-AC spaces to cut the heat.
A standalone air conditioning unit for spaces without built-in AC.

A tent or canopy structure providing shade/rain cover for an outdoor event.
A flat flooring surface laid over grass/uneven ground, needed for dance floors or heavy furniture outdoors.
Cabling and power points run across the venue so every vendor (lights, sound, catering) has power where needed.

Guest Comfort.includes: A self-serve water point so guests can hydrate without waiting on service staff.

A staffed area where guests can check in bags/coats during the event.
A basic first-aid station with supplies and someone trained to use them, on standby.

A grooming session covering hair styling, beard trim or basic grooming before the event.

Logistics.includes: Transport of decor/catering materials from the vendor to your venue.
Labour to load and unload equipment/materials at the venue, usually bundled with bigger setups.
A vehicle (and driver) shuttling guests to/from the venue, e.g. from a parking area or hotel.
Valet staff parking and retrieving guests' cars so they don't have to self-park.

Manpower.includes: Someone managing vendors and timing on the day, so you're not running the event yourself.
Oversight staff making sure setup and service run to plan, reporting issues as they happen.
Labour hands who physically assemble decor/furniture/equipment before the event starts.
Labour hands who take everything down and clear out after the event ends.
Security personnel managing entry, crowd and venue safety.
Staff doing ongoing cleaning during the event (spills, washrooms, trash) — separate from the post-event cleanup.
Staff checking guests in and guiding them to seating or activities.

Infrastructure.includes: A backup power generator for venues without reliable mains power, sized to your event's load.
A water-based air cooler for outdoor or non-AC spaces to cut the heat.
A standalone air conditioning unit for spaces without built-in AC.
A space heater for outdoor or cold-weather events to keep guests comfortable.
A tent or canopy structure providing shade/rain cover for an outdoor event.
A flat flooring surface laid over grass/uneven ground, needed for dance floors or heavy furniture outdoors.
Cabling and power points run across the venue so every vendor (lights, sound, catering) has power where needed.

Guest Comfort.includes: A self-serve water point so guests can hydrate without waiting on service staff.
A standalone restroom unit for outdoor venues without built-in washrooms.
A staffed area where guests can check in bags/coats during the event.
A basic first-aid station with supplies and someone trained to use them, on standby.

Safety.includes: Fire extinguishers placed at the venue as a safety requirement, especially where open flames or effects are used.
A trained first responder or paramedic on standby for the duration of the event.
Staff managing queues, entry flow and crowd density, especially for larger events.

Cleaning.includes: Cleaning the venue before setup begins, so decor goes into a clean space.
Full cleanup of the venue after the event ends, returning it to its original state.
Collection and removal of event waste/trash, rather than leaving it for the venue to handle.

A reserved section of the restaurant closed off for your group, with its own seating and privacy from other diners.
